briefing.headline: OpenAI and Google DeepMind accelerate frontier model releases as US-China AI competition intensifies.

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has entered a high-stakes phase with multiple labs deploying advanced reasoning systems. Funding remains robust while regulatory scrutiny grows. Multi-agent security vulnerabilities are emerging as a critical bottleneck.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with enhanced multi-agent orchestration. Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro both launched this week, while Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B. DeepSeek-R2 achieved parity on key benchmarks.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and IoT deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced a $9B expansion of its Arizona AI supercluster. TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips for NVIDIA and AMD. xAI activated its Memphis Colossus Phase 2 cluster.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI-level system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
